The night before the Hampi trip, Aparna sat on the sofa in her parents' Bengaluru flat with her laptop and her mother. 'Here's everything, Amma,' she said. She had typed the plan onto one page: overnight bus times, the guesthouse name, its address and phone number, the plan for both days, and the numbers of all five friends.
Amma read it twice. 'And this Mohit?'
'He's organising. His number's there. So is the guesthouse owner's.'
She printed a copy for the fridge and sent the file to her father, who was travelling. Then she opened the group chat and reminded everyone to keep sharing live location with each other until they were back.
Amma had been tight-lipped about the trip for a week. That night she only said, 'Call when you reach.' At 6:40 the next morning, Aparna did.

subtype: Approach: informing parents with itinerary and contacts [Action]
passage:
'Lokesh, did you send your parents the itinerary?'
'Why? I'm twenty. They'll just call every hour.'
'Mine used to. Then I started sending them everything before I leave. The stay address, the guesthouse number, the bus times, and one friend's number. Now they call once.'
'Seriously?'
'Seriously. When they know nothing, they imagine everything.' Jasleen held up her phone. 'Also, all of us are keeping live location on in the group till we're back from Mussoorie. Not for parents. For us.'
Lokesh frowned. 'What if I just tell my mum I'm going?'
'Then she has nothing to go on if your phone dies on a hill road.'
He was quiet for a moment. 'Okay. Send me your format.'
Jasleen forwarded it. That night Lokesh's mother replied to his message with a thumbs-up and 'Have fun, beta.'

qa.q: Why was Lokesh reluctant at first, and how did he feel?
qa.a: He felt irritated and wanted independence, expecting his parents to call every hour.

qa.q: What could Lokesh add if his phone battery is a worry?
qa.a: Carry a power bank and give his family a friend's number too, so someone can be reached if his phone dies.

qa.q: How might Lokesh's mother feel receiving the itinerary?
qa.a: She is likely relieved and trusting, replying 'Have fun, beta' instead of worrying.

grounding: Shows a student persuading a friend to share the itinerary, stay address and contacts with family and keep live location on for the group.
